title: Xanadu Secures Up to $10 Million in Additional DARPA Funding Under QBI Program - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Toronto-based photonic quantum computing company Xanadu Quantum Technologies (NASDAQ/TSX: XNDU) has received provisional approval for up to $10 million in additional non-dilutive contract funding under DARPA’s Quantum Benchmarking Initiative (QBI).

The one-year contract extension builds on Xanadu’s execution in Stage B of the QBI program. Under the agreement, Xanadu will deliver technical progress reports for DARPA’s ongoing architecture evaluations while allocating the majority of the funds to accelerate key hardware and software milestones across its fault-tolerant photonic R&D roadmap.

DARPA’s QBI program evaluates leading quantum computing approaches to verify whether candidate architectures can be constructed as designed and operated as intended to reach practical, utility-scale performance. Xanadu’s fault-tolerant architecture uses light to process quantum information, leveraging room-temperature compute operations and modular networkability demonstrated on its latest photonic system, Aurora.

The funding will also support the continued development of PennyLane, Xanadu’s open-source quantum software framework, while advancing the company’s hardware timeline toward useful, fault-tolerant commercial applications.
